Exercise C.B3 — Hard: Repeated use shares the same uncertain offset
    
      Average $100$ new corrected readings of the same fixed displacement after example 2. Their zero-mean noises are mutually independent and independent of the offset and calibration noises, each with variance $1\ \mathrm{mm}^2$. Find the average's error variance and its limiting value as the number of readings grows. Explain why the variance is not $(5/3)/100$.
      Review: variance and covariance; shared offset uncertainty.
      Show hintWrite the average error as one shared offset error plus an average of fresh noises. Only the second term is averaged away.
      Show worked solutionFor $n$ readings the average error is $(\theta-m)+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\varepsilon_i$. Independence gives variance $2/3+1/n$, hence $203/300\approx0.67667\ \mathrm{mm}^2$ at $n=100$. The limiting variance is $2/3$, with standard deviation about $0.8165$ mm. Distinct reading errors have covariance $2/3$ because they share the offset. Dividing each reading's entire variance by $100$ incorrectly assumes those errors are independent. Better calibration, rather than more repeated readings of an unknown displacement, is needed to reduce this uncertainty floor.

hypotheses: The source shared-offset model has priorN(0,4), two mutually independent Gaussian calibration noises of variances1 and4 independent of the prior, observations2 and-1, and correctionm=7/6. The conditional posterior is derived from that joint law, rather than assumed.

Conditioning at exact real readings uses the genuine normalized everywhere-positive density/Bayes kernel, whose disintegration is proved. An arbitrary version of a regular conditional law can differ at a zero-mass singleton; no uniqueness of every possible version at that singleton is asserted.
Fresh data is independent of the entire calibration model; its product law is preserved by the proved joint disintegration. All moment statements retain legitimate square-integrability domains.

For C.B3 the fresh noises may have arbitrary probability laws with zero means and genuine finite second moments/variance1. No Gaussian assumption is imposed on them. They are mutually independent and independent of the full prior/calibration data.

The number of readings is a positive integer; the source one-based sum is represented by all Fin n indices. The arbitrary-n limit uses the derived numerical variance formula, with the shared calibrated posterior held fixed.

The final calibration advice is scoped to this fixed-posterior model: averaging independent reading noise cannot change its shared-offset variance. It is not a universal impossibility theorem for other data or inference methods.
